name: Popular Science Quiz
description: How well do you science stuff?
author: ChatGPT

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?

answers.comment: Iron-rich dust gives Mars much of its reddish appearance.
Venus is covered by thick clouds and has an extremely hot surface.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

questions.question: What is the star at the centre of our Solar System?

answers.comment: Sirius is the brightest star in Earth's night sky.
The Sun is the star around which Earth and the other planets orbit.
Polaris is commonly known as the North Star.
Proxima Centauri is the nearest known star beyond our Solar System.

questions.question: What is Earth's natural satellite called?

answers.comment: Europa is a moon of Jupiter.
Titan is a moon of Saturn.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
Phobos is one of Mars's two moons.

questions.question: Which force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?

answers.comment: Friction resists motion between surfaces in contact.
Magnetism affects magnetic materials and moving electric charges.
Sound is a vibration that travels through a medium.
Gravity attracts objects with mass and governs planetary orbits.

questions.question: What is the process by which green plants use sunlight to make sugars?

answers.comment: Photosynthesis uses light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water.
Fermentation releases energy from sugars without requiring oxygen.
Digestion breaks down food into smaller substances.
Evaporation is the change from liquid to gas.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?

answers.comment: Ox is not the standard chemical symbol for oxygen.
Og is the symbol for oganesson.
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen.
C is the chemical symbol for carbon.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?

answers.comment: The liver processes nutrients and performs many chemical functions.
The heart contracts to circulate blood through the body and lungs.
The stomach helps break down food.
The kidneys filter blood and help regulate fluid balance.

questions.question: What is molten rock called while it is beneath Earth's surface?

answers.comment: Molten rock is called lava after it reaches the surface.
Granite is a type of solid igneous rock.
Quartz is a common mineral.
Molten rock beneath Earth's surface is called magma.

questions.question: Which of these travels fastest through a vacuum?

answers.comment: Sound requires a medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.
Light travels through a vacuum at about 300,000 kilometres per second.
An aeroplane travels far slower than light.
Ocean waves travel far slower than light.

questions.question: Which molecule carries most genetic information in living organisms?

answers.comment: Starch is a carbohydrate used for energy storage in plants.
Chlorophyll absorbs light for photosynthesis.
DNA stores hereditary instructions in almost all living organisms.
Haemoglobin carries oxygen in red blood cells.

questions.question: Which planet has the most prominent ring system?

answers.comment: Saturn's extensive rings contain mainly ice particles, along with rock and dust.
Earth does not have a prominent ring system.
Mars has no large, prominent ring system.
Venus has no prominent ring system.

questions.question: What is the unit of electrical resistance?

answers.comment: A watt measures power.
A volt measures electric potential difference.
An ampere measures electric current.
Electrical resistance is measured in ohms, symbol Ω.

questions.question: At room temperature, how would you describe a solution with a pH of 2?

answers.comment: A neutral aqueous solution is around pH 7 at room temperature.
A pH below 7 indicates an acidic solution.
Alkaline solutions have pH values above 7.
A low pH does not indicate that a solution is harmless.

questions.question: How many pairs of chromosomes are normally found in a human body cell?

answers.comment: This is fewer than the usual number in human body cells.
Human body cells normally contain 46 chromosomes in total, not 46 pairs.
Most human body cells contain 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs.
Human body cells contain many chromosome pairs.

questions.question: Which gas makes up the largest proportion of Earth's atmosphere?

answers.comment: Oxygen makes up about 21% of dry air.
Carbon dioxide is present in a much smaller concentration.
Hydrogen is present only in trace amounts in the lower atmosphere.
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of energy?

answers.comment: A newton is the SI unit of force.
The joule is the SI unit of energy and work.
A pascal is the SI unit of pressure.
A tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density.

questions.question: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?

answers.comment: Fluorine's chemical symbol is F.
Francium's chemical symbol is Fr.
Fe comes from the Latin name ferrum.
Fermium's chemical symbol is Fm.

questions.question: Which blood cells are primarily responsible for carrying oxygen?

answers.comment: White blood cells are important in immune defence.
Platelets help blood clot.
Stem cells can develop into specialised cells.
Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Solar System?

answers.comment: Andromeda is a neighbouring large galaxy.
Our Solar System is located in the Milky Way galaxy.
The Whirlpool Galaxy is a separate galaxy, also known as M51.
The Sombrero Galaxy is outside our own galaxy.

questions.question: Which two digits are used in the binary number system?

answers.comment: Standard binary notation uses 0 and 1.
These are the digits used in the decimal number system.
Binary is a base-2 system that uses only 0 and 1.
Letters are not used as the digits in standard binary notation.

questions.question: In a food chain, what is an organism that makes its own food, such as a green plant, called?

answers.comment: A predator hunts and eats other organisms.
Producers make organic food, often using energy from sunlight.
Decomposers break down dead organic matter.
A parasite obtains resources from a host organism.

questions.question: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?

answers.text: It needs a material medium to carry vibrations
answers.comment: Sound is a mechanical wave that travels through particles in a medium.

answers.text: Sound is made only of light
answers.comment: Sound and light are different types of waves.
Gravity does not block sound; a vacuum lacks particles to transmit it.
Temperature is not the reason sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negative electric charge?

answers.comment: Protons carry a positive electric charge.
Neutrons have no net electric charge.
Electrons carry a negative electric charge.
An alpha particle has a positive charge of +2.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin?

answers.comment: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile.
The spleen helps filter blood and supports immune function.
The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Specialised beta cells in the pancreas produce insulin.

questions.question: What is the main reason seawater tastes salty?

answers.comment: Sand is not the main cause of seawater's salty taste.
Seawater contains dissolved ions, including sodium and chloride.
Dissolved oxygen does not make seawater salty.
Organisms are not the main source of seawater's salty taste.

questions.question: A light-year is a unit used to measure what?

answers.comment: Despite the word 'year', a light-year measures distance.
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
Astronomers use other measurements to describe brightness.
Mass is measured in units such as kilograms.

questions.question: Which of these materials is strongly attracted to an ordinary magnet?

answers.comment: Glass is not strongly attracted to an ordinary magnet.
Dry wood is not strongly attracted to an ordinary magnet.
Iron is ferromagnetic and is strongly attracted to magnets.
Plastic is not strongly attracted to an ordinary magnet.

questions.question: Which scientist is most closely associated with the theory of evolution by natural selection?

answers.comment: Newton is best known for his laws of motion and universal gravitation.
Mendel's experiments helped establish the principles of inheritance.
Pasteur made major contributions to microbiology and germ theory.
Darwin presented influential evidence for evolution by natural selection.

questions.question: What is the change of state from a gas directly to a solid called?

answers.comment: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas.
Deposition is the direct change from gas to solid.
Melting is the change from solid to liquid.
Condensation is the change from gas to liquid.

questions.question: Which medical imaging technique uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves?

answers.comment: Magnetic resonance imaging uses magnetic fields and radio-frequency signals.
X-ray imaging uses ionising radiation.
Ultrasound imaging uses high-frequency sound waves.
Thermometry measures temperature rather than producing internal images.

questions.question: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which light cannot escape called?

answers.comment: The photosphere is the visible surface layer of a star.
An asteroid belt is a region containing many asteroids.
The event horizon marks the boundary beyond which escape is impossible.
A magnetopause is a boundary shaped by a magnetic field and surrounding plasma.

questions.question: Approximately how fast does light travel through a vacuum?

answers.comment: This is about one tenth of the speed of light.
This is far below the speed of light in a vacuum.
This is about ten times the actual speed.
Light travels at approximately 299,792 kilometres per second in a vacuum.

questions.question: What does an element's atomic number tell you?

answers.text: The number of protons in its nucleus
answers.comment: An element's atomic number is defined by its number of protons.

answers.text: The number of neutrons in every atom
answers.comment: Neutron numbers can vary between isotopes of the same element.
The number of electron shells is not the definition of atomic number.
Atomic number is not a measurement of mass.

questions.question: Which type of RNA carries genetic instructions from DNA to the cell's protein-making machinery?

answers.comment: Transfer RNA brings amino acids to the ribosome during protein synthesis.
Messenger RNA carries a genetic message used to make a protein.
Ribosomal RNA forms a key structural and functional part of ribosomes.
MicroRNAs mainly help regulate gene expression.

questions.question: What is the rigid outer layer of Earth, made up of the crust and uppermost mantle, called?

answers.comment: Earth's outer core is a liquid metallic layer deep inside the planet.
The asthenosphere is a softer region of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere.
The lithosphere includes the crust and rigid uppermost mantle and is divided into tectonic plates.
Earth's inner core is the solid central region.

questions.question: Which particle carries the electromagnetic force in the Standard Model of particle physics?

answers.comment: Gluons mediate the strong nuclear interaction.
Neutrinos interact mainly through the weak force and gravity.
The Higgs boson is associated with the Higgs field.
The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field.

questions.question: What does redshift in light from a distant galaxy usually mean?

answers.text: Its light has shifted towards longer wavelengths
answers.comment: Cosmological redshift is associated with the expansion of the universe.

answers.text: The galaxy must look red to the human eye
answers.comment: Redshift describes a wavelength shift, not simply an object's visible colour.
Redshift does not mean an object has stopped moving.

answers.text: The galaxy emits no visible light
answers.comment: Redshifted light can still be visible, depending on the amount of shift.

questions.question: What does a catalyst do in a chemical reaction?

answers.text: Always increases the maximum amount of product
answers.comment: A catalyst changes reaction rates, not the equilibrium yield under fixed conditions.

answers.text: Increases the reaction rate without being consumed overall
answers.comment: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.
Catalysts can be solids, liquids, gases or biological molecules.
A catalyst does not determine whether a reaction releases or absorbs heat.

questions.question: How do vaccines generally help protect the body against an infectious disease?

answers.text: They replace all white blood cells
answers.comment: Vaccines do not replace white blood cells.

answers.text: They kill every microbe in the body
answers.comment: Vaccines do not eliminate all microbes from the body.

answers.text: They train the immune system to recognise a pathogen or part of it
answers.comment: Vaccination helps establish immune responses and often immune memory.

answers.text: They work only by lowering body temperature
answers.comment: Lowering temperature is not how vaccines establish protection.

questions.question: Which part of a neuron commonly receives signals from other neurons?

answers.comment: Axon terminals commonly transmit signals to other cells.
Myelin insulates many axons and helps signals travel efficiently.
Red blood cells transport oxygen and are not neurons.
Dendrites commonly receive incoming signals from other neurons.

questions.question: What is an exoplanet?

answers.comment: Earth's Moon is a natural satellite within our Solar System.

answers.text: A planet orbiting a star beyond our Solar System
answers.comment: Exoplanets are planets outside our Solar System.

answers.text: An asteroid between Mars and Jupiter
answers.comment: Asteroids are small rocky bodies, not planets orbiting other stars.

answers.text: A star that has run out of fuel
answers.comment: A star's evolutionary stage does not make it an exoplanet.

questions.question: What is absolute zero on the Celsius temperature scale?

answers.comment: This is extremely cold but remains above absolute zero.
Zero Celsius is the freezing point of pure water under standard conditions.
Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, equivalent to −273.15 °C.
This is not the correct Celsius value; absolute zero is approximately −459.67 °F.

questions.question: What are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons called?

answers.comment: Ions have a net electric charge due to gaining or losing electrons.
Molecules consist of atoms chemically bonded together.
Allotropes are different structural forms of the same element.
Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.question: What does the term biodiversity mean?

answers.text: The variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels
answers.comment: Biodiversity includes variation within species, between species and among ecosystems.

answers.text: The number of rocks in an area
answers.comment: Rocks are not what biodiversity measures.

answers.text: The amount of rainfall in a habitat
answers.comment: Rainfall is an environmental factor, not biodiversity itself.

answers.text: The total mass of one species only
answers.comment: Biodiversity concerns variety rather than just the mass of one species.

questions.question: Which gas is a major contributor to the human-caused enhancement of the greenhouse effect?

answers.comment: Argon is not a significant greenhouse gas.
Human activities, including burning fossil fuels, have increased atmospheric carbon dioxide.
Neon is present in trace amounts and is not a significant greenhouse gas.
Helium is not a significant greenhouse gas.

questions.question: What is the main role of the Domain Name System (DNS) on the internet?

answers.comment: Encryption is provided by protocols and systems such as TLS, not DNS alone.
DNS is a naming system, not physical networking hardware.

answers.text: Translating domain names into IP addresses
answers.comment: DNS helps devices find the network addresses associated with domain names.

answers.text: Storing all websites on one central computer
answers.comment: Websites are hosted across many servers; DNS does not store all website content.

questions.question: Why are antibiotics ineffective against viruses that cause illnesses such as the common cold?

answers.text: Viruses are always larger than bacteria
answers.comment: Viruses are generally much smaller than bacteria.

answers.text: Antibiotics target bacterial structures or processes that viruses do not have
answers.comment: Viruses rely on host cells and lack many of the targets antibiotics act on.
Time of day is not why antibiotics fail against viruses.
Viruses contain genetic material, either DNA or RNA.

questions.question: Which object is classified as a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt?

answers.comment: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
The Sun is a star at the centre of our Solar System.
Europa is a moon of Jupiter.
Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune.

questions.question: What happens to a heavy atomic nucleus during nuclear fission?

answers.text: It splits into smaller nuclei, releasing energy
answers.comment: Fission splits a heavy nucleus and can release energy and neutrons.

answers.text: It combines with another nucleus to form a heavier one
answers.comment: That describes nuclear fusion in broad terms.
Fission does not turn a nucleus entirely into sound.

answers.text: It loses all its protons instantly
answers.comment: Fission does not involve every proton disappearing instantly.

questions.question: Who formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation?

answers.comment: Einstein developed the theories of special and general relativity.
Galileo made foundational contributions to the study of motion and astronomy.
Newton published these laws in his 1687 work Principia.
Faraday made major contributions to electromagnetism and electrochemistry.
